surprises.description: The preview expected only a reaffirmation of “late 2026” or possibly a named December window; Acumen specified that it expects to announce the ALTITUDE-AD topline results in November 2026, narrowing the timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Acumen confirmed it expects to announce top line Phase II ALTITUDE-AD results for sabirnetug in November 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch whether “late 2026” becomes a month (“December”), stays verbatim, or softens.

surprises.description: Acumen disclosed a specific bar for advancing sabirnetug to Phase III: approximately 30% slowing on the primary endpoint after 18 months. The preview discussed the readout and analysis plan but did not state a management success threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management set a success bar of approximately 30% slowing on the iADRS primary endpoint after the 18-month placebo-controlled period as the basis for advancing to Phase III.”

surprises.description: Management put a number on expected ARIA-E rates—low double digits—and said they may be consistent across genotypes. The preview flagged ARIA rates as important but gave no expected rate or genotype outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expects low double-digit ARIA-E rates that may be consistent across genotypes, supporting a potentially differentiated benefit-to-risk safety profile.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “safety including ARIA rates” and confirmation that “no blinded safety signal has surfaced.”

surprises.description: Q3 R&D expense was $21.1 million, above the preview’s $18.5 million estimate, despite the preview’s expectation that the prior JCR-related expense would roll off.
surprises.fact_evidence: “R&D expenses fell to $21.1 million in Q3 due to reduced manufacturing, materials, and CRO costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “R&D expense … $18.5M” and said the prior-quarter JCR charge had been expensed in Q2.

surprises.description: The $25.4 million net loss was larger than the preview’s $23.6 million estimate, though smaller than the roughly $31 million loss implied by consensus. The bottom-line result therefore differed depending on which preview benchmark is used.
surprises.fact_evidence: “R&D expenses fell to $21.1 million in Q3 … contributing to a net loss of $25.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Net loss ~$31M (implied)” and “My estimate: $23.6M.”

surprises.description: Primary-study retention reportedly exceeded expectations, and more than 95% of eligible patients consented to enter the open-label extension. The preview did not discuss these retention or rollover figures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Over 95% of eligible patients consented to roll over into the 12-month open-label extension, and primary study retention reportedly exceeded expectations.”

surprises.description: Management said it envisions one confirmatory Phase III after positive Phase II results and plans to include a subcutaneous formulation in that trial. The preview did not anticipate this specific development plan.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management envisions a single confirmatory Phase III following positive Phase II results and plans to incorporate a subcutaneous formulation into the Phase III, analogous to the LEQEMBI development path.”
